title: Lost Vikings fan remake, work in progress
author: domjjj
selftext:
One night, after good number of beers in at an arcade pub, we've touched on Lost Vikings in a discussion.

I had Codex remote on my phone and asked for a Lost Vikings inspired game, having the 3 escape an arcade pub after closing by having to go through the various arcades. This produced a functional, albeit fairly basic game.

Now, this is how it all started. However, it caught me. I loved the original game as a child and being able to come up with new puzzles was a dream come true. On top of that, this was a great test bed on how to produce pixel art games.

So far, the game was primarily built with GPT Sol 6.1 and GPT Image. Puzzle ideas are sometimes mine, sometimes of the AI or combination.

Few challenges I came across, and solutions:

* Animating consistent characters
   * Straight generated sprite sheets often suffered from animation glitches
   * Video generation can be a solution but I wanted to keep it within the Codex pipeline and pixel oriented
   * My current solution is using procedural sprite guides and then stylizing those with GPT Image (as seen in the video)
* Getting pixel elements to feel right
   * Used a pixel aligner so all generated art falls onto a real grid, using [https://github.com/Retro-Diffusion/pixel-art-fixer](https://github.com/Retro-Diffusion/pixel-art-fixer)
   * On top of it, added special contrast aware interpolation so hard edges stay sharp
   * Implemented multi loop agent creation and verification pipeline, which checks that objects are in the right size and fit the art style
* Having AI generate interesting puzzles and levels
   * Thinking through the puzzle and instructing precisely
   * And/or having the AI brainstorm with image gen before creating the level
* Making sure game remains playable and engaging
   * Automated level walkthroughs (every level comes with Playwright tests for various situations)
   * Review rules so puzzles are not repeated, use enough space and utilize all characters
   * Review rules for levels being dynamic
* Mobile usability
   * Thorough playtesting and targeted redesign prompts

  
The Fall and the Chase is a draft of a storyline that started to crystalize as I worked on the game. The Vikings find a strange object, that can create seemingly anything and it leads to something much larger and stranger.

Let me know what you think and if you'd like to see this story all the way until the end.

  
Live game: [https://vikings.domj.net/](https://vikings.domj.net/)

Repository: [https://github.com/domjancik/lost-vikings-fall-and-chase](https://github.com/domjancik/lost-vikings-fall-and-chase)
